title: Establish the Holdfast
summary: Our first job on launch day is not level 60. It is to get Holdfast operational: reach Stormwind, secure the guild name, open the bank, and put enough basic infrastructure under the founding roster that everyone else can start moving.

objectives.title: Secure the guild name
objectives.description: Start Human if you are willing, push into Stormwind, and be ready to create the guild immediately. Holdfast is our first choice, but fallback names need to be decided before launch.
objectives.need: Backup names and enough founders online to form the guild

objectives.title: Raise startup capital
objectives.description: Get the first gold online quickly. Skinning, mining, gathering, vendor trash, and disposable launch characters all count if they help us establish the guild and bank faster.
objectives.need: Early gatherers, skinners, miners, and fast liquid gold

objectives.title: Establish tailoring
objectives.description: Get tailoring online early and turn the first linen into useful carrying capacity. Starter bags and reagent bags are the first practical investment in the founding roster.

objectives.title: Open the guild bank
objectives.description: Once the guild exists, get shared storage operational and start moving useful materials out of individual inventories and into the common supply line.
objectives.need: Someone to own the first bank setup and deposits

objectives.title: Field the first dungeon groups
objectives.description: After the foundation is secure, people can settle into their mains. We do not need a race to level cap, but we do want tanks and healers reaching the first dungeon brackets early enough for guild groups to form naturally.

completeWhen: Guild secured. Bank operational. Founders supplied. First dungeon groups forming.
backlogSummary: Planned Missions stay visible before they become urgent. Rewards can be raised or lowered as Holdfast's needs change.

backlog.title: Welcome to Azeroth
backlog.description: Give genuine new players an unusually good first experience. The guild should actively reward veterans for teaching, grouping, explaining systems, and helping them clear early milestones.
objectives: First dungeon with patient guild mentors
Help through meaningful early progression walls

backlog.title: Integrate a New Recruit
backlog.description: Get new recruits into groups quickly, introduce them to people, and remove the friction that makes joining an established community awkward.
objectives: Invite them into an appropriate dungeon or activity
Connect them with players near their level and goals
Help with immediate profession or gearing friction

backlog.title: Alt Support
backlog.description: Helping alts is still useful guild activity, but it should not pull the same incentives as onboarding a true newcomer or integrating a fresh recruit.
objectives: Fill difficult group quests when convenient
Help complete targeted dungeon or gear goals
Keep rewards modest unless the alt fills a strategic guild need

backlog.title: Build the Supply Line
backlog.description: Once the founding scramble settles, identify the materials and profession coverage Holdfast actually lacks and put stronger incentives behind the shortages that matter.
objectives: Assign targeted gathering and crafting goals
Increase rewards when a shortage becomes strategically important
backlog.rewardBasis: Raised when help is scarce or strategic

rewardPolicy: Official Missions may award Reputation and Service Marks. Reputation is permanent and never spent. Service Marks can later be spent through member support requests. Member-funded requests redistribute Marks but never create Reputation.
